skill.name: reactome-database
skill.description: Query Reactome REST APIs for pathway retrieval, enrichment analysis, gene-to-pathway mapping, species projection, and pathway browser links for systems biology research.
skill.summary: Analyze Reactome pathways, identifiers, enrichment results, and browser links from structured API guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Reactome documentation URLs, Markdown code fences, and expected API examples. I found no prompt injection attempt or malicious intent. The remaining risks are external submission of biological identifiers, token exposure in output, and a helper script output path that can overwrite input files.

remediation.issue: Output file can overwrite input data
remediation.suggestion: Generate output paths with pathlib, require an explicit output option, and refuse to write when input and output paths match.

remediation.issue: Biological identifiers are submitted to Reactome
remediation.suggestion: Document the external data transfer clearly and warn users not to submit restricted or patient-derived data without approval.

remediation.issue: Analysis tokens appear in terminal and saved results
remediation.suggestion: Treat Reactome tokens as sensitive, redact them from routine logs, and store result files in approved project locations.
Add request timeouts and clear retry behavior to avoid indefinite waits during Reactome API failures.

content.value_statement: Pathway analysis requires exact Reactome endpoints and valid data formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through queries, enrichment, and result interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Reactome Content Service and Analysis Service endpoints.
Shows REST requests for database version, entity lookup, and pathway molecules.
Guides overrepresentation and expression analysis with gene lists or TSV data.
Maps identifiers to human pathways using projection endpoints.
Provides a Python helper for version, query, search, entities, and analysis commands.
Builds Reactome Pathway Browser URLs from analysis tokens.
limitations: Requires network access to reactome.org for live queries.
Analysis submissions may send gene or expression identifiers to Reactome.
The helper script does not implement retries, rate limiting, or output overwrite protection.
The reactome2py package is described as functional but not actively maintained.

use_cases.title: Interpret Gene List Enrichment
use_cases.description: Run a Reactome overrepresentation workflow and summarize significant pathways with p-values and FDR values.

use_cases.title: Inspect Pathway Membership
use_cases.description: Look up a Reactome pathway and summarize participating proteins, complexes, reactions, and species context.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible API Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable REST API steps for pathway queries, species projection, token reuse, and browser links.

prompt_templates.title: Check Database Version
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Reactome database skill to find the database version endpoint and explain the expected result.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Query pathway R-HSA-69278 with Reactome guidance and summarize its name, species, entity types, and relevant molecules.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Gene Enrichment
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these identifiers with Reactome overrepresentation guidance: TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC, CDK1. Return significant pathways and FDR values.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Projection Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Reactome workflow for mouse identifiers that projects results to human pathways, stores tokens safely, and summarizes browser links.

output_examples.input: A list of cancer-related gene symbols for enrichment analysis.
output_examples.output: A ranked pathway summary with pathway names, identifiers, p-values, FDR values, matched entities, and a browser link.

output_examples.input: A Reactome stable identifier such as R-HSA-69278.
output_examples.output: A plain-language pathway profile with name, species, schema class, participating molecules, and related reactions.

output_examples.input: Mouse gene identifiers that need human pathway projection.
output_examples.output: A projection workflow that explains the endpoint, submitted data format, token handling, and interpretation steps.

best_practices: Review gene lists for sensitive or unpublished data before submitting them to Reactome.
Cache analysis tokens only in approved project storage and delete them when no longer needed.
Use batch submissions and filter results by FDR before interpreting biological significance.
anti_patterns: Do not submit patient-derived or restricted datasets without authorization.
Do not treat pathway enrichment as proof of causation without biological validation.
Do not run the helper script on a file path that lacks a clear output plan.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps query Reactome pathways, run enrichment analysis, map identifiers, and interpret pathway browser results.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Live pathway queries and analysis requests require network access to reactome.org.

faq.question: Can it analyze expression data?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance explains Reactome TSV input requirements for expression analysis.

faq.question: Can it map non-human identifiers?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents projection endpoints for mapping identifiers to human pathways.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python helper script for common Reactome query and analysis commands.

faq.question: What data should users avoid submitting?
faq.answer: Users should avoid submitting restricted, patient-derived, or unpublished biological data without approval.
